IANS New Delhi, Japanese investor SoftBank Group has sold 1.65 per cent stake in Meesho for Rs 1,885 crore, further trimming its investments in India's e-commerce sector. In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to Rs 1,885.17 crore. With this, the affiliate's holding in Meesho has fallen to 5.19 per cent from 6.84 per cent. The stake sale , however, found buyers, with a clutch of domestic and foreign institutional investors participating in the transaction, with Societe Generale (SocGen) emerging as the largest buyer. Live Events Paris-based financial services firm SocGen picked up more than 1.47 crore shares, or a 0.32 per cent stake, for Rs 364.65 crore. Domestic institutional buyers included mutual funds managed by Motilal Oswal, HDFC, Edelweiss and Aditya Birla Sun Life, along with Bajaj Life Insurance. Overseas participants included Morgan Stanley, Fidelity Investments, BNP Paribas, Goldman Sachs, Ghisallo Capital Management, William Blair Investment Management and Texas Municipal Retirement System. The Singaporean government, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Norway's sovereign wealth fund Government Pension Fund Global, also participated in the transaction. Meesho shares rose 1.53 per cent to close at Rs 257.99 apiece on the NSE on Friday. The latest transaction adds to a series of stake sales by SoftBank in its Indian portfolio companies, particularly in the e-commerce and consumer technology space. Earlier this month, the Japanese investor pared a 1.56 per cent stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions for Rs 1,896 crore. Before that, in September, it sold a 1.7 per cent stake in Meesho for Rs 1,650 crore. SoftBank had also divested nearly a 2.6 per cent stake in Lenskart for Rs 2,888 crore in August and a further 3.25 per cent stake for Rs 2,873 crore in June. In January, the technology investor reduced its shareholding in electric two-wheeler maker Ola Electric Mobility by 2.15 per cent, continuing its broader portfolio monetisation exercise in the country. Agencies Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions on Thursday said it has committed Rs 50,000 crore investment in Andhra Pradesh to develop 3GW integrated power generation facilities across wind, solar and pumped hydro . According to a company statement, Clean Max has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board (APEDB) in this regard. Under the MoU, CleanMax proposes to invest nearly Rs 50,000 crore to develop integrated power generation facilities aggregating 3 GW of clean energy across wind and solar energy and 1 GW of pumped hydro facilities. The power will be supplied to a compute factory being set up at Kurnool in collaboration with Neysa, with Clean Max responsible for the power infrastructure and supplies. Razorpay filed draft documents with Sebi via the confidential route in June for an IPO. Sembcorp Green Infra filed preliminary papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) in August to raise up to Rs 3,750 crore through an IPO. After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations to Razorpay and Sembcorp Green Infra on November 3 and November 13, respectively, the update showed. The company serves millions of businesses across India, ranging from startups and small and medium enterprises to large corporates. Razorpay attained unicorn status in 2020 and has since expanded beyond payments into a broader financial services ecosystem for businesses. Its offerings enable merchants to manage collections, payouts, payroll, cash flows and access to capital through a single platform. The company is backed by investors like Peak XV Partners, GIC , Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital and TCV. The confidential filing route allows companies to submit draft offer documents to Sebi for review without immediately disclosing sensitive business information to the public.
